messages:
incident-bot: PAGING: Severity=P1 region=us-west-2 — Multiple AZs reporting elevated 5xx and partial routing blackholes. Auto-alert threshold hit (latency and error-rate). Runbook: <https://redwood.internal/runbooks/multi-region-failover|multi-region-failover>. @sre-oncall you are now on-call.

olivia: acked. seeing ~40% of prod traffic still hitting us-west-2a while health checks show instances drained in that AZ. some requests 502/504. customers reporting slow API and timeouts.

 tj: on it. are routes failing or is it LB/ASG misconfig? checking LB backends and route53 health checks now.

 priyanka: adding context — automated draining started after a scheduled maintenance in us-west-2a. canaries were passing earlier then spikes started ~5m ago.

 sre-oncall: got it. i'm running `curl -v https://api.redwood.com/health` from us-west-2b and eu-west-1 to compare. also checking BGP/route advertisements and edge caches.

 infra-bot: Deploy bot: Canary rollout 2026-03-15T03:02Z completed in us-west-2a at 1719009600. No rollback events.

 olivia: logs show many `connection reset by peer` from the edge proxies in us-west-2a. also seeing `503 Service Unavailable` from upstream with KV-cache errors.

 tj: route53 status: primary weighted record for api.redwood.com still points 100% to us-west-2. health checks show 2/3 failing for us-west-2a but overall region health=degraded. attempting to increase TTL to 10s and shift weight to us-east-1 now.

 priyanka: careful — previous automated traffic-shift failed and created oscillation. we need a controlled shift with canary percentages: 10 -> 30 -> 60. Also verify model-serving pool capacity in target region.

 sre-oncall: agreed. starting manual traffic-shift:
```
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z12345 --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"api.redwood.com","Type":"A","SetIdentifier":"us-east-1","Weight":10,"TTL":10,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"34.200.123.45"}]}}]}'
```

 mike: FYI, autoscaler reports burst capacity in us-east-1 is at 30% free. we can absorb initial 10% but need to watch queue lengths.

 olivia: applying traffic-shift now. switching canary to 10%. monitoring latency and 5xx.

 sre-oncall: canary at 10% propagated. immediate metrics: 5xx overall drop 12%, but us-west-2a still receiving ~35% traffic due to stale edge caches.

 tj: edge caches TTLs at CDN layer are 60s, but some POPs still have stale mapping. filing ticket with CDN ops: CDN-3456 — request flush / accelerate mapping update for api.redwood.com. @cdn-support please prioritize.

 infra-bot: CDN flush request sent to provider (ticket CDN-3456). estimated propagation 45-90s.

 priyanka: given stale caches, we should also add an immediate routing policy fallback: set origin failover to prefer us-east-1 when health < 70%. initiating change now.

 sre-oncall: applied failover policy change. watch for oscillation. enabling `safe-shift` that waits 60s at each step and requires 3 consecutive good health-check samples before advancing.

 olivia: good — canary to 30% after 2m if 5xx stays down and latency normal. currently 5xx trending down across regions.

 tj: customer impact: monitoring incidents channel shows 18 customer support pings, 2 ongoing escalations. reaching out to accounts team to notify affected customers and offer status.

 mike: running `kubectl get pods -n prod -o wide` in us-west-2a: many pods Ready=1/2; imagepull backoff on sidecars observed. suspect sidecar crashing and causing upstream 502s. dumping pod logs.

 olivia: sidecar crash reason: OOMKilled in the new sidecar version -> memory regression. that explains partial unhealthy backends. rolling sidecar rollback to previous revision in us-west-2a.

 sre-oncall: rollback issued for sidecar in us-west-2a. command: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/proxy-sidecar -n prod --to-revision=12`. watching pod replacement and health checks.

 infra-bot: Rollout undo acknowledged. Kubernetes events show new pods starting at 1719010280.

 tj: rollback successful; backend health checks recovered to 3/3 in us-west-2a but edge cache still routing some requests for a bit. 5xx rate now near baseline.

 priyanka: removing manual traffic-shift controls and returning to automatic weighted routing after verifying 10m stable. we should keep safe-shift policy in place for 30m.

 olivia: customer impact summary for postmortem: ~18 customers affected, median latency increase 400ms, peak error rate +3.8% for 27 minutes. major cause: sidecar memory regression + CDN cache TTLs causing stale routing while region was being drained.

 sre-oncall: next steps: incident writeup, include timeline, root cause (sidecar regression + inadequate canary rollback detection + CDN cache mismatch), action items: stricter canary resource limits, automatic rollback on OOM patterns, reduce CDN mapping TTL for critical endpoints, and add additional guard to safe-shift controller.

 olivia: assigning action owners: priyanka -> canary/rollback automation; mike -> sidecar memory regression investigation + fix; tj -> CDN TTL/edge mapping process; sre-oncall -> postmortem doc + customer impact email draft.

 incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: Status=Mitigated. Severity downgraded to P3. Full incident timeline: <https://redwood.internal/incidents/1719009999|view>.

 sre-oncall: closing thread for live coordination. moving to postmortem channel for writeup. thanks all for quick responses. :thumbsup:
